newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Cautious Russian MinFins firm, eye Yeltsin, US data.
newsitem.headline: Cautious Russian MinFins firm, eye Yeltsin, US data.

text.p: MinFin bond prices rose slowly after falling late on Wednesday on news President Boris Yeltsin was in hospital with pneumonia, dealers said on Thursday.
They added trading was cautious with the market awaiting further news about Yeltsin and U.S. payroll data due on Friday.
MinFins like other emerging market paper track U.S. Treasuries, and so are affected by U.S. statistics.
Yeltsin was taken back to hospital late on Wednesday for treatment for pneumonia, but his doctors said his temperature was normal.
"New York hit prices strongly yesterday. But today people realised nothing terrible has happened and are buying steadily," a Russian bank dealer said.
He added prices could recover to Wednesday's early levels later today or tomorrow.
Dealers said the fourth and fifth tranches were bid the most but trading was still cautious.

"There is uncertainty on the market as U.S. interest rates could go up after payrolls. Yeltsin's health is another reason for that. But still everybody considers MinFins undervalued at current levels," Sberbank dealer Pavel Sool said.
